headline: President: No more 'Aynaghar' or secret detention centres in Bangladesh
summary: President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir pledges justice for victims of enforced disappearances and promises a future without secret prisons.
details: President Mirza Fakhrul Islam Alamgir has pledged to ensure justice for victims of enforced disappearances, stating that Bangladesh will never again allow secret detention centres, known as 'Aynaghar', to exist.

Speaking at an event marking the International Day of the Victims of Enforced Disappearances 2026, the President declared that all those involved in these crimes would face the highest punishment under the law.
The President emphasized that the state must also take responsibility for the rehabilitation, healthcare, and social security of families who suffered years of uncertainty and financial hardship.

He described enforced disappearance as a crime against humanity and a grave violation of human rights, noting that such practices were used to silence dissent and protest against injustice over the past 15 years.
Referring to a Commission of Inquiry report, he cited 1,569 incidents of enforced disappearance, with 287 victims found to have been killed.

To prevent future occurrences, the Enforced Disappearance Prevention and Remedy Bill, 2026 has been placed before Parliament, and Bangladesh has signed the International Convention for the Protection of All Persons from Enforced Disappearance.
The President called for a pursuit of justice rather than revenge, stressing that state power must remain under the control of the Constitution and the law.

headline: 967 dead as measles outbreak kills 4 more in 24 hours
summary: The Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS) reports a surge in suspected measles cases across Bangladesh, with over 157,000 infections suspected.
details: Four more people died within the last 24 hours due to measles symptoms, bringing the total death toll to 967, according to a report by the Directorate General of Health Services (DGHS).
The DGHS data reveals that 99 deaths were confirmed cases of measles, while 868 people died with measles-like symptoms.
In the last 24 hours alone, 1,516 people exhibited symptoms of the virus, adding to a massive total of 157,194 suspected infections across the country.
The outbreak is continuing to spread across various regions of Bangladesh, with health authorities monitoring the situation closely.
